question: Will Russia capture Prymorske by September 30, 2026?
rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the intersection at 47.623814° N, 35.288073° E in Prymorske, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

The intersection will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces continued limited offensive operations west and south of Orikhiv on September 16 and 17 but did not advance.

evidence.publisher: Ukrinform, citing the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
evidence.excerpt: A total of 278 combat engagements between the Ukrainian Defense Forces and Russian forces were recorded along the front line over the past day, September 16. Ukrinform reports this, citing the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine in a Facebook update on the situation as of 8:00 on Thursday, September 17. In the Orikhiv sector, Ukraine’s Defense Forces stopped one Russian attempt to advance toward Prymorske.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Russian forces recently advanced southwest of Orikhiv. Russian forces advanced in southeastern Novoandriivka (west of Orikhiv), according to geolocated footage published on September 16.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Ukrainian forces have held Russian forces to near-zero net gains since March 2026, and have conducted successful counterattacks in the Kupyansk, Oleksandrivka, and now Lyman directions. Russian forces have made limited but significant gains in and around Kostyantynivka and east of Slovyansk and Kramatorsk, but are fighting to maintain momentum in these areas and elsewhere along the front line.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: A Russian milblogger acknowledged on August 8 that Russian forces no longer maintain positions in southern Prymorske (west of Orikhiv).

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Geolocated footage published on June 2 and June 3 shows Ukrainian forces striking Russian-occupied buildings in southern Mala Tokmachka (southeast of Orikhiv) and southern Prymorske (northwest of Orikhiv) after what ISW assesses were infiltration missions.

evidence.publisher: Institute for the Study of War
evidence.excerpt: Assessed Ukrainian advances: Recent video and textual evidence, including geolocated footage published on March 19, 24, and 25, indicates that Ukrainian forces liberated northern and central Prymorske and Richne (both northwest of Orikhiv).
